title: Mattermost Automation: Integrations Guide (2026)
summary: Mattermost automation sends and receives messages via webhooks, slash commands, and bots. Learn which setup method works best for your needs.
body_markdown:
## Add slash commands and webhooks


In both cases[Mattermost](https://mattermost.com/blog/mattermost-server-surpasses-20000-stars-on-github/) sends the request to a URL you control, and the answer depends on code you maintain. That puts the history of the behaviour in your repository too.


**Slash commands have a 3-second limit** and outgoing webhooks 30 seconds, so if your code takes longer it'll timeout.


### Create the command and set the Request URL


Go to Integrations, then Slash Commands, then Add. The form wants a title, a description, and a trigger word without the leading slash, so` deploy` becomes` /deploy` .


Of everything on the form, the Request URL is the field that matters, the endpoint Mattermost calls when someone runs the command. Set the method to POST unless your endpoint only accepts GET.


The autocomplete hint and description are optional, but without them nobody learns what arguments the command takes.


### Slash command response format and JSON reply


When someone runs the command, Mattermost posts form data to your URL, including the channel, the user name, and everything typed after the trigger word. Reply with JSON.


The` text` field is the message, and` response_type` decides who sees it:` in_channel` posts for everyone,` ephemeral` shows only the person who ran the command.


On a normal day, any handler that queries a slow API will time out, because a Mattermost slash command waits about[3 seconds](https://forum.mattermost.com/t/solved-outgoing-webhook-timeout-time/4013) , the same as Slack's. **Return a short acknowledgement at once, then do the work and post the result afterwards.**


### Outgoing webhooks versus slash commands


**Nobody types a slash with an outgoing webhook** , which makes it passive. You register trigger words, a channel, or both, and Mattermost POSTs to your callback URL whenever a message matches. Your JSON reply appears in the channel as a response to that message.


That changes two things. First, a trigger word fires for anyone who says it in conversation, so a common word will call your server constantly. Pick distinctive words.


Second, the patience is longer: Mattermost gives outgoing webhooks[30 seconds](https://forum.mattermost.com/t/solved-outgoing-webhook-timeout-time/4013) , **ten times the slash-command window** , so operations that take longer won't timeout. That's enough for a modest lookup, but a build or a report can still outrun it.


Choose the slash command when a person is asking for something on purpose. Choose the outgoing webhook when the message itself is the signal. In both cases, anything slower than the window needs the quick acknowledgement first.


When the slow work behind that acknowledgement means calling several other apps, Activepieces has a Mattermost connector among its 750 integrations.


That count is taken from the folders in the` packages/pieces/community` directory of the open-source monorepo on GitHub, whose core is MIT-licensed, and roughly 60% of those connectors were contributed by the community, which means features get built for real problems, not just vendor priorities.


If the app you need isn't there, the code is open to read and extend.
